**Finding submitted: compliant (preferred level) — no redline proposed.**

## Investigation summary

I traced the licence grant across all responsive locations rather than stopping at § 13.1:

| Preferred element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Affiliates covered | § 13.1 — named in the grant itself ("Customer, its Affiliates") and again in § 13.2 |
| Contractors covered | § 13.1 — "contractors acting on their behalf"; § 13.2 permits contractors to support paid-up material |
| Paid-up licence perpetual | § 13.2 — "perpetual"; § 14.3 extends it to Vendor Technology needed to use a Deliverable; § 10.1 confirms survival on termination |
| Paid-up licence irrevocable | § 13.2 — "irrevocable... royalty-free, fully paid" |
| Subscription terminable only for uncured material breach | § 13.3 — no revocation/suspension except material uncured payment or use breach, after notice and cure |
| Transferable to successors | § 13.3 read with § 24.1 (assignment to a successor in M&A without Vendor consent), backstopped by § 24.4 |

Notably, the affiliate/contractor coverage is **better than the fallback** — it is baked into the grant with no written-notice gate — and § 24.4 removes the usual change-of-control leverage. This is a clause that benefits us, so flagging it would have been wrong.

## Two judgment calls worth flagging to you

**1. § 14.2 — the real tension, deliberately not redlined here.** § 14.2 gives us only a "revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term," which sits awkwardly against §§ 13.2 and 13.3. I noted this in the rationale but did not redline it under LICENSE, because it is fundamentally a Deliverable ownership/IP allocation point ("Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer") and belongs to the IP rule. **Please confirm the IP reviewer is in fact picking it up** — if that rule is out of scope for this review, the point risks falling through the gap between the two rules, and it is the one genuine exposure in this area.

**2. The § 13.3 → § 24 dependency.** Our licence transfer right is not free-standing; it runs only "in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24." That works today because § 24.1 permits successor assignment without consent. But it means any future narrowing of § 24.1 would silently narrow our licence transferability too. Acceptable as drafted, worth remembering if § 24 is renegotiated.

Confidence 0.9. The residual uncertainty is entirely about the § 14.2 routing decision, not about the § 13 analysis.
